subject: Preemptible standby — RTO/RPO SLA exception request
messages:
From: Marcus Jennings <m.jennings@finvault.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Li <s.li@finvault.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Preemptible standby — request for SLA exception

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. To follow up from our side: FinVault is interested in a lower-cost standby option in APAC that would use preemptible instances (short-lived capacity) for non-critical workloads and a warm-standby for core services.

High level ask: would Redwood consider a formal SLA carveout so FinVault can accept a longer RTO window (target ~4 hours) and a slightly looser RPO (up to 30 minutes) for the preemptible standby tier in APAC in exchange for a 25% reduction on the regional standby commitment cost? We can accept a narrower liability cap for that tier.

Attached is a brief request form and an ops diagram (SLA_Exception_Form.pdf, FinVault-preemptible-ops-diagram.png). Primary concerns are: activation lead time, detection & automated failover behavior, and runbook handoffs.

Can you confirm if Redwood has a formal process for approving these sorts of exceptions, what mitigations you would require (monitoring, playbooks, escalation path), and an estimated timeline for review?

Thanks,
Marcus Jennings
Director of Infrastructure
FinVault

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Jennings <m.jennings@finvault.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Preemptible standby — request for SLA exception

Marcus — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Short answer: yes, we can consider a temporary SLA amendment for a preemptible standby tier in APAC, provided certain mitigations are in place. I want to outline what we'll need from both sides and propose next steps.

Requirements from Redwood side (high level):
- Documented activation procedure (who runs the switchover, runbook link).
- Synthetic health checks and automated detection hooks to reduce mean time to detect.
- Snapshotting / warm cache schedule to keep RPO near your 30-minute target as much as possible.
- Predefined rollback and fallback policy (what falls back to hosted vs. dedicated).

What we need from FinVault:
- Confirmation on which service tiers you want on the preemptible standby (full stack vs. select APIs).
- A single technical point-of-contact for runbook drills.
- Agreement on a short list of committed engineers to join failover drills (first three exercises within 60 days of exception approval).

Operational mitigations we can offer as part of the exception:
- 24/7 routed on-call during high-risk windows for the first 90 days.
- Required warm snapshot cadence (every 15 minutes for critical caches, 60 minutes otherwise).
- A standby activation SLA of 4 hours (from detection to traffic cutover) for preemptible tier; we would keep standard 60-minute RTO for your core dedicated tier.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik will provide an engineering feasibility note and an adjusted RTO/RPO acceptance matrix.
2) Legal will draft an SLA amendment template with liability carveouts.
3) If acceptable, we run a tabletop drill and then a live failover test.

I'll loop in legal and ops for review; copying Karthik and Grace now.

—Aditya
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Jennings <m.jennings@finvault.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Preemptible standby — request for SLA exception

Marcus, Aditya — quick tech note from infra/serving runtime:

Feasibility: preemptible nodes are supported, but they introduce two failure modes we need to explicitly mitigate: preemption storms (many nodes reclaimed) and longer cold-start penalty for large models. For FinVault's APIs that require sub-200ms p99 latency, we recommend keeping those on dedicated pools. For batch/async and lower-QPS endpoints, preemptible standby makes sense.

Recommended configuration for the exception:
- RTO target: 4 hours (detection -> verified traffic cutover).
- RPO target: 15–30 minutes depending on persistence tier; we can guarantee 15 min for DB snapshots (additional cost), 30 min for in-memory cache via frequent warmed snapshots.
- Warm pool: maintain a small, non-preemptible control plane (2 pinned instances) to manage orchestration and accelerate reinstatement.
- Canary ramp: staged cutover (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over the 4-hour window to limit blast radius.

Operational costs/credits: to compensate for longer RTO we can propose a 20% credit on standby capacity for the first 6 months, reviewed afterwards. The final discount will be contingent on runbook adherence and results of the first live failover.

I've attached a short tech spec (RTO_RPO_Tech_Specs.xlsx) that maps your services to recommended RPO bands. If FinVault confirms the exact service list, we can produce a scoped amendment.

Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Jennings <m.jennings@finvault.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Preemptible standby — request for SLA exception (legal review)

Team — I reviewed the requested carveout. Key legal points to include in the SLA amendment (drafting notes):

1) Explicitly state the preemptible tier is "Best Effort" with an activation SLO of 4 hours; do not label as equivalent to standard Redwood SLA.
2) Liability cap: reduce from standard service credit model to a fixed capped credit equal to 15% of one month's standby commit for the affected region, with language that excludes consequential damages.
3) Term & review: exception granted for a 6-month pilot, with mandatory operational review after 90 days and termination clause if drills/failovers fail twice.
4) Data handling: confirm snapshot retention and encryption controls; FinVault must confirm any longer retention beyond standard.
5) Required runbook and three tabletop exercises to be completed within 60 days of amendment execution.

I'll produce a redline of the amendment and the short-form exception exhibit. Aditya, please confirm who signs for the commercial amendment and whether we need CSM acceptance language.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Jennings <m.jennings@finvault.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Preemptible standby — request for SLA exception (approval & conditions)

All — after reviewing Karthik's feasibility note and Naomi's legal redline, I approve a conditional exception for FinVault's preemptible standby in APAC under these conditions:

1) Pilot duration: 6 months starting on the amendment effective date.
2) RTO/RPO: 4 hour activation SLA; RPO 15–30 minutes depending on service class as defined in the Tech Spec.
3) Financial: 20% standby credit for first 6 months, contingent on successful drill #1 within 45 days.
4) Operational prerequisites: committed FinVault POC, completed runbook, scheduled tabletop and one live failover (rollforward/rollback plan must be validated).
5) Termination triggers: two failed live failovers or missed drill commitments will revert the account to standard standby requirements and remove the credit.

Aditya — please proceed to send the amendment exhibit and coordinate signatures. Marcus — we'll target the tabletop for week-of Jan 11 and the first live failover the week after, pending your availability.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Global Operations
Redwood Inference
